speaker: Volunteer A
turns: What brought you to the garden?
I only came for vegetables at first. Now I stay to help the next person get started.
How do you decide what needs doing?
The rules said to water only our own plots. When my neighbor missed a week, I watered theirs too. I did not want their plants to suffer.
Has helping changed how you feel here?
People say thank you, which makes me feel part of the garden. Sometimes I worry that if I stop helping, I will not feel welcome.

speaker: Volunteer B
turns: What does a usual visit look like?
I check the shared watering list before my own plot. It is easier to join in when someone has written down what needs doing.
The plot borders help me know where to start, but they are not a reason to leave a dry plant alone. We talk and work things out.
Is there anything you would change?
I like helping, but the same few people always do the extra jobs. I wish we could ask for a quiet week without having to explain ourselves.
